mechanism: Both drugs affect gastrointestinal motility through different mechanisms—semaglutide delays gastric emptying via GLP-1 receptor agonism while scopolamine reduces GI motility via anticholinergic effects—potentially resulting in additive gastrointestinal effects and unpredictable drug absorption.
action: Monitor for excessive GI dysfunction (severe constipation, gastric retention); consider alternative anticholinergic agents or ensure adequate spacing of administration with careful clinical observation.
